Chapter 5: Living Out Faith in a World of Injustice.
If you look around, you’ll notice—the world just isn’t how it should be. There’s injustice, cruelty, and a lot of indifference, almost everywhere you turn. And honestly, it’s easy to feel powerless. Sometimes, it seems like nothing will ever change.
That’s when many people just turn away, focusing on their own lives, figuring someone else will handle the world’s problems.
But here’s what’s different when faith is real. It simply can’t stay quiet when there’s injustice. Faith calls for a response. It stirs something inside you—to stand up, to speak out, and to take action. And let’s be real, that’s not easy. Sometimes it means going against the crowd, putting your reputation, your comfort, maybe even your safety, on the line.
Picture this: you see a colleague being treated unfairly at work. The easy thing? Stay silent. Don’t rock the boat. But something deep down won’t let you ignore it. So you speak up—even though you know there could be consequences. Maybe some people are grateful, but others? They’re angry. There’s a real cost to doing what’s right, but there’s also a powerful sense of integrity that comes from it.
The truth is, living out faith in a world full of injustice isn’t about making huge, dramatic gestures. It’s about those small, everyday choices—to do what’s right, especially when it’s tough. It’s refusing to just accept things as they are, and believing that change can happen, even when it feels like the odds are stacked against you.
And here’s something beautiful: when communities take this calling seriously, they become beacons of hope. They support each other, they refuse to be silent, and together, they show that justice isn’t just an idea—it’s something you can actually see and feel in the way people live.
